questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted something different, and as I applied the "leftover" spots, there weren't many spots that I believed qualified as being very different from Denmark. Furthermore, I picked Spain because of the weather, culture and the people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Universidad de Granada was very good at making the transition smooth and the orientation was very thorough.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had to orientation meetings, one for the whole university and one for the faculty of political science. We were offered mentors, and easy access to the Internalization Office

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are Facebook groups, Whatsapp groups and other means available, but I just booked an AirBNB, which was very cheap for a long term stay. I saw that many of my friends were scammed by their landlords in terms of not getting their deposit back; high utilities etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be very aware of your contracts: Utilities are very expensive so make sure there's room for that in your budget (if they aren't included in your rent).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I signed up for classes when i applied for the university, but you can also change your courses within the first month. I didn't do that, so I don't know how that works

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The internalization office was very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A groups are morning classes and B groups are evening classes (I had classes till 22, which was very unexpected)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 4 4th year courses and 1 3rd year courses, and they were not too difficult

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. The classes were more "high school" like and not lecture based.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Political systems in the Maghreb, Sistema político y juridico en la UE, Política Comparada, Theory of democracy: Gender and interculturality, International organizations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Many of my courses were very disappointing as some of the teachers were very unstructured and sometimes just didn't show up for class (Theory of democracy), and the teaching style was often very monotone and indifferent. I would recommend Political systems in the Magreb, the EU course and Política Comparada. The latter two ONLY if the future students speak spanish.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Granada is insanely cheap, and I did not have any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In Granada you get free tapas when your order drinks, so you spend very little money on food - with that said groceries are not that much cheaper compared to DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are Erasmus organizations that plan everything that your heart could ever desire including sports, social activities, cultural trips, etc. The school also offers sport activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some of the Erasmus groups as they are a great way to meet new people and experience Granada. There's also a Spanish school where you can learn Spanish, and I hear great things about that school (Center of Modern Languages)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other cities close to Granada, go hiking in Sierra Nevada or join events with the Erasmus groupss

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me the cultural shock was very intense and it took me at least 2 months to get used to it. But I think this goes for any place that isn't your home country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There is a pretty big language barrier, so it is best if you speak Spanish; if not there are not a lot of Spanish students who are proficient in English

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Constant car honking; language barrier; more rudeness towards strangers compared to Denmark; often not very good service

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The life of the city and the sense of community that was very apparent

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Speak or learn to speak Spanish
- The classes are based a lot on active participation, so there are many presentations, papers and seminars that are mandatory
- Some courses have different groups with different teachers. The individual teacher can decide on the exam, and whether or not there should be an exam. Research which group has the exam

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a very accommodating university, and if any questions should arise, the University is very helpful. I didn't personally take any sociology classes, but I know the "Sociology of Life" course wasn't very popular amongst my friends who took it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning Spanish, at least well enough to pass my Spanish exams

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, I had two Spanish courses and I only started learning Spanish in the Spring of 2023. This was very stressful, and even my friends who were way better at Spanish than me also struggled. So I would say only choose Spanish courses if you are actually comfortable speaking and listening to Spanish.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
